A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, tables, figure, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching despite revisions and repagination.

before.justification: Appendix F reports original neural-network experiments on binary MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, and a synthetic parity task, including measured training and test errors.

after.justification: Appendix F retains these original experiments and adds temperature settings and numerical comparisons with Mou et al.’s generalization bound.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 newly proposes optional objective adaptations: smooth loss clipping, such as c tanh(L/c), and additional c||theta||² regularization. The underlying CLD/SGLD procedures and retained experimental architectures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that these adaptations were used experimentally.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same binary image-classification tasks and 70-bit, three-coordinate parity task. The new Appendix F.3 comparison reuses binary MNIST without introducing different task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Mou et al.’s bound, already included in the analytical comparison in Table 1, becomes a numerical comparator in new Appendix F.3 and Tables 5–8. The comparator membership of Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Tables 2–4 expand the temperature grid. New Tables 5–8 evaluate binary MNIST at 20, 50, 250, and 400 epochs; the comparator calculation uses the continuous-time Mou bound, sets s=0.5, and omits its log log M term. The retained experiments’ architectures, learning rates, and training durations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The additional temperature rows extend the existing noise-sensitivity analysis. Appendix F.3 additionally examines how relative bound tightness varies with temperature and training duration. The existing parity analysis is retained, with its discussion moved into F.2.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ± reporting in Tables 2–4 and shaded bands in Figure 1, without defining the spreads or specifying run counts and seeds. The new comparison tables provide point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add five temperature rows and revise bound values, while matched training and test errors remain unchanged. For example, the MNIST bound at beta=0.03N changes from 0.10461 to 0.10498. New Tables 5–8 report setting-dependent rankings between the proposed bound and Mou et al.’s bound.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.7 changes N>1 to N≥8, replaces ln(1/delta) with ln(N/delta), and changes the square-root denominator from N to 2N; Corollary 3.1 also receives the logarithmic revision. Appendix B replaces the asserted parameter-optimization route with a derivation through the previously present PAC-Bayes-kl bounds and Pinsker’s inequality, refines the tighter bounds, and adds Lemma B.5 with proof. Appendix A revises the pointwise second-law proof, while D.1/H.2.1 explicitly state the curl-free condition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding summary retain the central contribution: time- and trajectory-independent generalization guarantees for Markov processes with Gibbs stationary distributions, specialized to temperature-controlled CLD. The rewritten introduction does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds discussion of infinite initial-loss suprema, differentiable clipping, and the claimed cost of stronger regularization. Appendix F.3 newly qualifies comparative tightness: either bound can be tighter depending on temperature and training duration. The existing limitations concerning discretization and non-isotropic noise remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 newly specifies Gaussian initialization with variance 1/d_in, lambda=d_in, and regularization coefficient lambda/beta. This clarifies implementation of the previously reported regularized dynamics rather than establishing a changed setting. F.3 also documents its comparator calculation.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused citations and discussion concerning implicit bias, optimization, loss clipping, and single-sample PAC-Bayes guarantees. Section 4.3 expands the SGLD comparison, including Pensia et al., Negrea et al., and Dadi and Cevher. The central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten, an appendix roadmap is added, Appendix B is organized into four subsections, and the parity discussion moves into F.2. Explanatory footnotes, acknowledgments, and the venue header are added or updated. The overall section and appendix sequence remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–8 and expands Tables 2–4 with additional rows. Figure 1 is resized and reformatted while retaining its panels and legend. The single-column format and Table 1 structure are preserved, with local changes to spacing and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the main guarantees easier to assess through the revised PAC-Bayes derivation, explicit diffusion assumption, and additional proof details. The qualified numerical comparison with Mou et al. and initialization disclosure also improve the supporting evidence. These gains are limited by remaining inconsistencies: the abstract does not reflect the revised logarithmic term, and experimental spreads and run counts remain unexplained.
